sections.overview: The Aru Flying Fox is a bat in the family Pteropodidae, currently treated as a living species from Indonesia.
sections.identification: It belongs to the flying-fox genus Pteropus; a taxonomic treatment notes a whitish back as a distinctive feature.
sections.habitat: Its known type locality is the Aru Islands in Indonesia; published species-specific habitat information is limited.
sections.diet: The sources reviewed for this species do not provide a documented species-specific diet.
sections.behavior: Species-specific behavior is poorly documented in the sources reviewed.
sections.reproduction: The reviewed sources do not describe its reproductive biology.
sections.ecology: The Mammal Diversity Database treats Pteropus aruensis as a valid species; older sources discussed it as a form of the Black-bearded Flying Fox, Pteropus melanopogon.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database reports it as Critically Endangered; its limited documentation counsels caution about claims on its present population.
